g.font-family: Arial, 'Noto Sans CJK SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif
g.text: ONE EXAMPLE · FOUR RESEARCH SKILLS
What does an AI researcher do?
Suppose training scores improve, but performance on new tasks stays flat.
This is an example, not an experimental result.
RESEARCH TASTE
1 Choose a useful question
Why is there no gain on new tasks?
Read earlier work. Explain what is unknown
and why answering it would matter.
Output: a question and why it matters
QUESTIONS & HYPOTHESES
2 Make the idea testable
Better data, or simply more training?
List possible explanations and what
we would expect to see if each is right.
Output: explanations and an experiment plan
RESEARCH EXECUTION
3 Test the explanations
Compare data choices on new tasks.
Keep training conditions comparable. Record
uncertainty, failed runs, and repeatable steps.
Output: evidence for or against each explanation
LEARNING FROM EXPERIENCE
4 Improve the next study
Does the lesson help on a new task?
Save what worked, what failed, and when.
Test whether these lessons improve later work.
Output: lessons tested on a new task
CHECK RESEARCH QUALITY
Is the question worthwhile? Is the finding new?
Does the evidence hold up? Where does it apply?
New evidence can change the question or method. Return to an earlier step when needed.
